title: suggest `sf` instead of depend
description: There are probably good reasons for that but the fact that this package depends on `sf` makes `gganimate` inderectly depends on `sf` which means people have to install GDAL, GEOS, PROJ4, etc. before they can animate a bar plot. Would it make sense for `transformr` to only suggest `sf` ?

title: Inconsisent id numbers in tween_sf
description:
Im running into an error when running the tween_sf function on a pair of sf polygons. For many of the pairs, the function works great, well done! However, for some polygons, there is an issue when assigning ids towards the end of the function sequence. I've tracked this down to the following sequence:
[polys.zip](https://github.com/thomasp85/transformr/files/13181697/polys.zip)

`poly1  <- read_sf("poly1.shp")
poly2  <- read_sf("poly2.shp")
df1 <- data.frame(geo = poly1  %>% st_as_sfc())
df2 <- data.frame(geo = poly2  %>% st_as_sfc())

polys <- tween_sf(poly1, poly2, ease="linear", nframes=5)
### line 24 in tween_sf
morph[which(sf_columns)] <- tween_sf_col(sf_from, sf_to, 
                                           rep("linear", length.out = ncol(from))[sf_columns], nframes)
### line 3 in  tween_sf_col
aligned <- align_sf(from[[i]], to[[i]])
### line 15 in align_sf
aligned <- Map(function(from, to, type) {
    switch(type, POINT = , 
MULTIPOINT =align_sf_point(from, to), 
LINESTRING = , 
MULTILINESTRING =align_sf_path(from, to, 50), 
POLYGON = , 
MULTIPOLYGON = align_sf_polygon(from, to, 50))
 }, from = from, to = to, type = from_type)
### line 13 in align_sf_polygon
to$id <- id`

which throws the error:  Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "id", value = c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,  : 
  replacement has x rows, data has y

In this example, the issue is with poly2, but I cannot determine why. I have tried poly2 %>% st_simplify(), poly2 %>% st_make_valid(), etc. With simplify, the number of rows in the above error message will change, but the error is still thrown. I have also tried varying the ease function and the number of transitions, but this doesnt help.

title: Issue tweening polygons with two holes
description:
The code below uses `tween_polygon` to morph a triangle into a letter. This works for all letters except those that consist of two holes, such "g" or "B".  (In this font, the lowercase "g" consists of two holes.)

With the assist of [@Z.lin](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54848190/difference-between-ggplot-and-grid-picture-with-complex-shapes) I was able to use `geom_polypath` to successfully plot these two hole letters. 

I think I need `ggplot`'s `group =` option to be two things at the same time. 

group = id
1)  This tells objects with id = 1 to morph into other objects with id = 1. If the objects have two holes, however, they are plotted incorrectly because we lose the section information that `geom_polypath` requires to plot objects with multiple holes. 

OR

group = section
2) This results in a confused morph. However, objects with two holes are plotted correctly. 

Is there a way to have both things at the same time? A morph with id = 1 morphing into objects with id = 1 and `geom_polypath` using the `group = section` option so that two-holed letters are drawn correctly?

________________________________________________________________
letter_g file is located [here](https://www.dropbox.com/s/d2zztc79v43ubdm/letter_g?dl=0)

```
library(tidyverse)
library(transformr)
library(tweenr)
library(gganimate)
library(ggpolypath)

get_letter <- function(){
        # Read Postscript info for letter
        letter_xml <- readRDS("letter_g")

        # Extract coordinates from Picture object
        x <- letter_xml@paths$text@letters[1]$path@x
        y <- letter_xml@paths$text@letters[1]$path@y
        
        one_letter <- tibble(
                x, 
                y,
                x.n = names(x),
                id = 1
        )
}

segment_scale_letter <- function(one_letter){
        
        # Segment polygon
        one_letter <- one_letter %>%
                mutate(is.move = x.n == "move") %>%
                mutate(section = cumsum(is.move)) %>%
        
                group_by(section) %>%
                mutate(section.length = n()) %>%
                ungroup() %>%
                filter(section.length >= 3)
        
        # Scale letter so max(height), max(width) match [0, 1]
        one_letter$x <- one_letter$x - min(one_letter$x)
        one_letter$y <- one_letter$y - min(one_letter$y) 
        
        one_letter$x <- one_letter$x / max(one_letter$x)
        one_letter$y <- one_letter$y / max(one_letter$y) 
        
        one_letter <- select(one_letter, x, y, id, section)
}

do_morph <- function(df1, df2){
      tween_polygon(df1, df2,
                    ease = 'linear', 
                    nframes = 12, 
                    id = id)  
}

do_plot <- function(morph){
        ggplot(morph) +
                geom_polypath(aes(x = x, y = y, group = id)) +
                transition_time(time = .frame) +
                theme(legend.position = "none") +
                scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 4)) +
                scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-2, 2))
}

do_gif <- function(ani){
        animate(ani, nframes = 60, fps = 30, width = 900, 
                renderer = gifski_renderer(loop = FALSE), start_pause = 15)
}

# Shape df  
df1 <- data.frame(
        poly_star(n = 3, st = FALSE)
)
df1 <- mutate(df1, section = df1$id)

# Letter df
one_letter <- get_letter()
df2 <- segment_scale_letter(one_letter)

morph <- do_morph(df1, df2) 
plot <- do_plot(morph)  
ani <-  do_gif(plot)

ani

# This plots the 'g' perfectly 
# ggplot(df2) +
#         geom_polypath(aes(x = x, y = y, group = section))
```
